front: Hello! How are you doing today? (formal, m)
back:
Namaste! Aaj aap kaise hain?

Namaste! Āj āp kaise haiṁ?

Namaste (Hello) | Āj (today) | āp (you - formal) | kaise (how) | haiṁ (are)

front: Everything is going great on my side.
back:
Mere side par sab badhiya hai.

Mere side par sab baṛhiyā hai.

Mere side par (on my side) | sab (everything) | baṛhiyā (great/good) | hai (is)

"Mere" instead of "merā" because of "par" after "side"

front: I live in Toronto right now.
back:
(Main) abhi Toronto me rahta hoon.

(Maiṁ) abhī Toronto meṁ rahtā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | abhī (right now) | Toronto meṁ (in Toronto) | rahtā hūṁ (live - male)

front: No. I don't understand English. (m)
back:
Ji nahi, main angrezi nahi samajhta hoon.

Jī nahīṁ, maiṁ aṅgrezī nahīṁ samajhtā hūṁ.

Jī nahīṁ (No) | maiṁ (I) | aṅgrezī (English) | nahīṁ (not) | samajhtā hūṁ (understand - male speaker)

front: I understand a little Hindi.
back:
Main thodi thodi hindi samajhta hoon.

Maiṁ thoṛī thoṛī hindī samajhtā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | thoṛī thoṛī (a little bit) | hindī (Hindi) | samajhtā hūṁ (understand - male speaker)

front: Are you American?
back:
Kya aap amriki hain?

Kyā āp amrīkī haiṁ?

Kyā (Are/question marker) | āp (you - formal) | amrīkī (American) | haiṁ (are)

front: Yes.
back:
Ji haan.

Jī hāṁ.

Jī hāṁ (Yes - polite)

front: Today I am a bit busy with work.
back:
Aaj main work ke saath thoda busy hoon.

Āj maiṁ work ke sāth thoṛā busy hūṁ.

Āj (today) | maiṁ (I) | work ke sāth (with work) | thoṛā (a bit) | busy hūṁ (am busy)

front: By the way, what are you up to? (informal, f)
back:
Vaise, tum kya kar rahi ho?

Vaise, tum kyā kar rahī ho?

Vaise (by the way) | tum (you) | kyā (what) | kar rahī ho (are doing - female)

front: I am working at my office desk right now.
back:
Main abhi apne office desk par kaam kar raha hoon.

Maiṁ abhī apne office desk par kām kar rahā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | abhī (right now) | apne office desk par (at my office desk) | kām (work) | kar rahā hūṁ (am doing - male)

*Note: "apne" is used instead of "merā" because the subject (Maiṁ) is acting on his own desk. "Apnā" shifts to "apne" before "par".

front: I work in the AI field.
back:
Main AI field me kaam karta hoon.

Maiṁ AI field meṁ kām kartā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | AI field meṁ (in AI field) | kām kartā hūṁ (work - male habitual)

front: Are you free this weekend? (casual)
back:
Kya tum is weekend free ho?

Kyā tum is weekend free ho?

Kyā (Question marker) | tum (you) | is weekend (this weekend) | free ho (are free)

Kyā turns the whole sentence into a yes/no question, it's like "are" or "is" or "will".

front: Actually, I am ready to leave.
back:
Vaise, main nikalne ke liye ready hoon.

Vaise, maiṁ nikalne ke liye ready hūṁ.

Vaise (actually/by the way) | maiṁ (I) | nikalne ke liye (to leave) | ready hūṁ (am ready)

front: No worries, everything will be fine.
back:
Tension mat lo, sab theek ho jayega.

Tension mat lo, sab ṭhīk ho jāegā.

Tension mat lo (don't worry) | sab (everything) | ṭhīk ho jāegā (will become fine)

front: I practice playing the guitar every evening.
back:
Main har evening guitar practice karta hoon.

Maiṁ har evening guitar practice kartā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | har evening (every evening) | guitar practice kartā hūṁ (do guitar practice - male)

front: I am learning a new song on the piano right now.
back:
Main abhi piano par ek naya song seekh raha hoon.

Maiṁ abhī piano par ek nayā song sīkh rahā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | abhī (right now) | piano par (on piano) | ek nayā song (a new song) | sīkh rahā hūṁ (am learning - male)

front: I play video games with friends on weekends.
back:
Main weekends par friends ke saath video games khelta hoon.

Maiṁ weekends par friends ke sāth video games kheltā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | weekends par (on weekends) | friends ke sāth (with friends) | video games kheltā hūṁ (play video games - male)

front: What kind of music do you listen to? (informal)
back:
Tum kis type ka music sunte ho?

Tum kis type kā music sunte ho?

Tum (you) | kis type kā (what kind of) | music (music) | sunte ho (listen to)

front: I like spending time outdoors in Toronto.
back:
Mujhe Toronto me bahar time spend karna pasand hai.

Mujhe Toronto meṁ bāhar time spend karnā pasand hai.

Mujhe (to me) | Toronto meṁ (in Toronto) | bāhar (outdoors) | time spend karnā (spending time) | pasand hai (is liked)

front: I am working on a software coding project.
back:
Main ek software coding project par kaam kar raha hoon.

Maiṁ ek software coding project par kām kar rahā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | ek software coding project par (on a software coding project) | kām kar rahā hūṁ (am working - male)

front: I usually get free from work around (1-10) PM.
back:
Main usually (ek/do/teen/char/panch/cheh/saat/aath/nau/das) PM ke paas work se free hota hoon.

Maiṁ usually (ek/do/tīn/chār/pāñch/chhah/sāt/āṭh/nau/das) PM ke pās work se free hotā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | usually (usually) | 5 PM ke pās (around 5 PM) | work se (from work) | free hotā hūṁ (get free - male)

front: Are you watching any good show these days? (informal, m)
back:
Kya tum aajkal koi accha show dekh rahe ho?

Kyā tum ājkal koī acchā show dekh rahe ho?

Kyā (Question marker) | tum (you) | ājkal (these days) | koī acchā show (any good show) | dekh rahe ho (are watching)

front: I am learning Hindi because I want to chat with my friends.
back:
Main Hindi seekh raha hoon kyunki main apne friends ke saath chat karna chahta hoon.

Maiṁ Hindī sīkh rahā hūṁ kyoṅki maiṁ apne friends ke sāth chat karnā chāhtā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | Hindī sīkh rahā hūṁ (am learning Hindi - male) | kyoṅki (because) | maiṁ (I) | apne friends ke sāth (with my friends) | chat karnā (to do chat) | chāhtā hūṁ (want - male)

front: That sounds like a great plan!
back:
Ye toh bahut achha plan lag raha hai!

Ye toh bahut acchā plan lag rahā hai!

Ye (this) | toh (indeed/emphasis) | bahut acchā plan (very good plan) | lag rahā hai (is sounding/seeming)

front: I want to visit Norwich this October.
back:
Main is October Norwich visit karna chahta hoon.

Maiṁ is October Norwich visit karnā chāhtā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | is October (this October) | Norwich visit karnā chāhtā hūṁ (want to visit Norwich - male)

"is" October instead of "ye" because months take oblique demonstrative

front: I need some coffee before starting work.
back:
Mujhe work start karne se pehle thodi coffee chahiye.

Mujhe work start karne se pahle thoṛī coffee chāhiye.

Mujhe (I/to me) | work start karne (to start work) | se pahle (before) | thoṛī coffee (some coffee) | chāhiye (need)

front: Can you help me with this task?
back:
Kya tum meri is task me help kar sakte ho?

Kyā tum merī is task meṁ help kar sakte ho?

Kyā (Question marker) | tum (you) | merī (my) | is task meṁ (in this task) | help kar sakte ho (can help - male/general)

front: I can speak a little bit of Hindi now.
back:
Main ab thodi si Hindi bol sakta hoon.

Maiṁ ab thoṛī sī Hindī bol saktā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | ab (now) | thoṛī sī Hindī (a little bit of Hindi) | bol saktā hūṁ (can speak - male)

front: I really like this cocktail.
back:
Mujhe ye cocktail bahut pasand hai.

Mujhe ye cocktail bahut pasand hai.

Mujhe (I/to me) | ye cocktail (this cocktail) | bahut pasand hai (really like)

"ye" instead of "is" because no postposition on "cocktail"

front: I don't know about that topic.
back:
Mujhe us topic ke baare me nahi pata.

Mujhe us topic ke bāre meṁ nahīṁ patā.

Mujhe (to me) | us topic ke bāre meṁ (about that topic) | nahīṁ patā (don't know)

"us" is the oblique case of "vo" because of "ke"

front: Do you want to grab a beer with me tonight? (informal, m)
back:
Kya tum aaj raat mere saath beer peena chahte ho?

Kyā tum āj rāt mere sāth beer pīnā chāhte ho?

Kyā (Question marker) | tum (you) | āj rāt (tonight) | mere sāth (with me) | beer pīnā chāhte ho (want to drink beer)

front: I need to transition into a new career role soon.
back:
Mujhe jaldi ek naye career role me transition karna hai.

Mujhe jaldī ek naye career role meṁ transition karnā hai.

Mujhe (I) | jaldī (soon) | ek naye career role meṁ (into a new career role) | transition karnā hai (have to transition)

front: I can play both guitar and piano.
back:
Main guitar aur piano dono bajaa sakta hoon.

Maiṁ guitar aur piano donoṁ bajā saktā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | guitar aur piano donoṁ (both guitar and piano) | bajā saktā hūṁ (can play instrument - male)

front: I want to catch up with Shivani after a long time.
back:
Main bahut time (ke) baad Shivani se catch up karna chahta hoon.

Maiṁ bahut time (ke) bād Shivani se catch up karnā chāhtā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | bahut time bād (after a long time) | Shivani se (with Shivani) | catch up karnā chāhtā hūṁ (want to catch up - male)

Shivani *se* because it's a two-way interaction/communication, not physical accompaniment like with "ke sāth"

front: Yesterday was a very productive day at work.
back:
Kal work par bahut productive day tha.

Kal work par bahut productive day thā.

Kal (yesterday) | work par (at work) | bahut productive day (very productive day) | thā (was)

front: How was your day in Norwich today? (informal, m)
back:
Aaj Norwich me tumhara din kaisa tha?

Āj Norwich meṁ tumhārā din kaisā thā?

Āj (today) | Norwich meṁ (in Norwich) | tumhārā din (your day) | kaisā thā (how was)

front: I understood what you explained.
back:
Main samajh gaya jo tumne explain kiya.

Maiṁ samajh gayā jo tumne explain kiyā.

Maiṁ (I) | samajh gayā (understood - male) | jo (what/which) | tumne explain kiyā (you explained)

front: I didn't understand that sentence properly.
back:
Main wo sentence sahi se nahi samjha.

Maiṁ vo sentence sahī se nahīṁ samjhā.

Maiṁ (I) | vo sentence (that sentence) | sahī se (properly) | nahīṁ samjhā (did not understand - male)

front: When did you leave your software job at Ford? (informal)
back:
(Tumne) Ford me software job kab chhodi?

(Tumne) Ford meṁ software job kab chhoṛī?

Tumne (you) | Ford meṁ (at Ford) | software job (software job) | kab (when) | chhoṛī (left)

front: Where did you go for dinner yesterday? (Informal, m)
back:
Tum kal dinner ke liye kahan gaye?

Tum kal dinner ke liye kahāṁ gaye?

Tum (you) | kal (yesterday) | dinner ke liye (for dinner) | kahāṁ (where) | gaye (went - male/plural)

Because jānā (to go) is an intransitive verb, ne is never used with it.

front: I worked on my new coding project yesterday evening.
back:
Maine kal evening apne naye coding project par kaam kiya.

Maine kal evening apne naye coding project par kām kiyā.

Maine (I) | kal evening (yesterday evening) | apne naye coding project par (on my new coding project) | kām kiyā (did work)

front: We had so much fun during our university days!
back:
Hamare university days me humne bahut maza kiya!

Hamāre university days meṁ hamne bahut mazā kiyā!

Hamāre university days meṁ (in our university days) | hamne (we) | bahut mazā kiyā (had so much fun)

front: What happened at the care home today?
back:
Aaj care home me kya hua?

Āj care home meṁ kyā huā?

Āj (today) | care home meṁ (at the care home) | kyā huā (what happened)

front: I will call you tomorrow evening.
back:
Main kal evening tumko call karunga.

Maiṁ kal evening tumko call karūṅgā.

Maiṁ (I) | kal evening (tomorrow evening) | tumko (you) | call karūṅgā (will call - male)

front: We will meet in Norwich this October!
back:
Hum is October Norwich me milenge!

Hum is October Norwich meṁ mileṅge!

Hum (we) | is October (this October) | Norwich meṁ (in Norwich) | mileṅge (will meet)

front: I will reach the coffee shop in 10 minutes.
back:
Main 10 minutes me coffee shop pahunchunga.

Maiṁ 10 minutes meṁ coffee shop pahuñchūṅgā.

Maiṁ (I) | 10 minutes meṁ (in 10 minutes) | coffee shop (coffee shop) | pahuñchūṅgā (will reach - male)

front: How is your job as a lifestyle coordinator going? (Informal, f)
back:
Tumhari lifestyle coordinator ki job kaisi chal rahi hai?

Tumhārī lifestyle coordinator kī job kaisī chal rahī hai?

Tumhārī (your) | lifestyle coordinator kī job (lifestyle coordinator job) | kaisī chal rahī hai (how is it going)

front: I will try my best to learn fluent Hinglish before October.
back:
Main October se pehle fluent Hinglish seekhne ki poori try karunga.

Maiṁ October se pahle fluent Hinglish sīkhne kī pūrī try karūṅgā.

Maiṁ (I) | October se pahle (before October) | fluent Hinglish sīkhne kī (to learn fluent Hinglish) | pūrī try karūṅgā (will try my full best - male)

front: Tell me everything about your new life in the UK! (informal, f)
back:
Mujhe UK me tumhari nayi life ke baare me sab batao!

Mujhe UK meṁ tumhārī naī life ke bāre meṁ sab batāo!

Mujhe (to me) | UK meṁ (in the UK) | tumhārī naī life ke bāre meṁ (about your new life) | sab batāo (tell everything)

front: I am very excited to visit you in October.
back:
Main October me tumse visit ke liye bahut excited hoon.

Maiṁ October meṁ tumse visit ke liye bahut excited hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | October meṁ (in October) | tumse visit ke liye (to visit you) | bahut excited hūṁ (am very excited - male)

front: We will definitely grab a drink together when I arrive.
back:
Jab main aaunga, hum zaroor saath me ek drink peeyenge.

Jab maiṁ āūṅgā, hum zarūr sāth meṁ ek drink pīyeṅge.

Jab (when) | maiṁ āūṅgā (I arrive - male) | hum (we) | zarūr (definitely) | sāth meṁ (together) | ek drink pīyeṅge (will drink a drink)

front: It will take some time, but it will be great!
back:
Thoda time lagega, lekin bahut achha hoga!

Thoṛā time lagegā, lekin bahut acchā hogā!

Thoṛā time lagegā (it will take a little time) | lekin (but) | bahut acchā hogā (it will be very good)

front: Are you free tomorrow for a drink?
back:
Kya kal tum drink ke liye free ho?

Kyā kal tum drink ke liye free ho?

Kyā (Question marker) | kal (tomorrow) | tum (you) | drink (drink) | ke liye (for) | free (free) | ho (are)

front: What's up? Everything is fine. (chal)
back:
Kya chal raha hai? Sab badhiya hai.

Kyā chal rahā hai? Sab baṛhiyā hai.

Kyā (What) | chal rahā hai (is running/going on) | Sab (everything) | baṛhiyā (fine/great) | hai (is)

front: Excuse me, how are you? I'm fine, but I don't understand Hindi very well.
back:
Suniye, aap kaise hain? Main achha hoon, magar main Hindi bahut achha nahi samajhta hoon.

Suniye, āp kaise haiṁ? Maiṁ acchā hūṁ, magar maiṁ Hindī bahut acchā nahīṁ samajhtā hūṁ.

Suniye (Excuse me) | āp (you) | kaise (how) | haiṁ (are) | Maiṁ (I) | acchā (good/fine) | hūṁ (am) | magar (but) | maiṁ (I) | Hindī (Hindi) | bahut (very) | acchā (good/well) | nahīṁ (not) | samajhtā hūṁ (understand - male)

front: Where is the restaurant? It's not here, it's over there on Main Street.
back:
Restaurant kidhar hai? Vo idhar nahi hai, vo udhar Main Street par hai.

Restaurant kidhar hai? Vo idhar nahīṁ hai, vo udhar Main Street par hai.

Restaurant (Restaurant) | kidhar (where/which way) | hai (is) | Vo (It/That) | idhar (here) | nahīṁ (not) | hai (is) | vo (it/that) | udhar (over there) | Main Street (Main Street) | par (on) | hai (is)

front: Do you want to eat lunch now, or do you want to eat later? (informal, f)
back:
Kya tum abhi lunch khaana chaahti ho, ya baad me khaana chaahti ho?

Kyā tum abhī lunch khānā chāhtī ho, yā bād meṁ khānā chāhtī ho?

Kyā (Question) | tum (you) | abhī (now) | lunch (lunch) | khānā (to eat) | chāhtī ho (want - female) | yā (or) | bād meṁ (later) | khānā (to eat) | chāhtī ho (want - female)

front: Do you want to drink some coffee with me? (informal, f)
back:
Kya tum mere saath kuch coffee peena chaahti ho?

Kyā tum mere sāth kuch coffee pīnā chāhtī ho?

Kyā (Question) | tum (you) | mere sāth (with me) | kuch (some) | coffee (coffee) | pīnā (to drink) | chāhtī ho (want - female)

front: I also wanted to buy something.
back:
Main bhi kuch khareedna chaahta tha.

Maiṁ bhī kuch kharīdnā chāhtā thā.

Maiṁ (I) | bhī (also) | kuch (something) | kharīdnā (to buy) | chāhtā thā (wanted to - male)

front: What time is the meetup? / We will meet at 4 PM.
back:
Meetup kitne baje hai? / Hum 4 baje milenge.

Meetup kitne baje hai? / Hum 4 baje mileṅge.

Meetup (meetup) | kitne baje (what time) | hai (is)? / Hum (we) | 4 baje (at 4 o'clock) | mileṅge (will meet - plural/formal)

front: Ivargal / Avargal
back:
Ye log / vo log

Ye log / vo log

Ye log (these people / they [near]) | vo log (those people / they [far])

front: Yesterday I came to see you but you weren't here. So today I came to see you again.
back:
Kal main tumse milne (ke liye) aaya lekin tum yahaan nahi the. Isliye aaj main fir se tumse milne aaya.

Kal maiṁ tumse milne (ke liye) āyā lekin tum yahāṁ nahīṁ the. Isliye āj maiṁ phir se tumse milne āyā.

Kal (Yesterday) | maiṁ (I) | tumse (you - with/to) | milne (to meet - oblique shift) | āyā (came - past) | lekin (but) | tum (you) | yahāṁ (here) | nahīṁ the (were not) | Isliye (So / That's why) | āj (today) | maiṁ (I) | phir se (again) | tumse (you - with/to) | milne (to meet - oblique shift) | āyā (came - past)

front:
• I eat.
  • I am eating.
  • I ate.
  • I will eat.

I eat: Main khaata hoon.

Maiṁ khātā hūṁ (eat - habitual) | Maiṁ khā rahā hūṁ (eating - continuous) | Maine khāyā (ate - past transitive) | Maiṁ khāūṅgā (will eat - future)

front: (all pronouns) need coffee
back:

Mujhe (I/to me) | Tujhe/Tujhko (you - intimate) | Tumheṁ/Tumko (you - casual) | Āpko (you - formal) | Ise/Isko (this person / him / her [near]) | Use/Usko (that person / him / her [far]) | Humeṁ/Humko (we / to us) | Unheṁ/Unko (they / to them) | coffee chāhiye (need coffee)

front: Making a new song tonight will be fun.
back:
Aaj raat naya gaana banaana fun hoga.

Āj rāt nayā gānā banānā fun hogā.

Āj rāt (tonight) | nayā (new) | gānā (song) | banānā (making/to make) | fun (fun) | hogā (will be)

front: What nonsense is happening? I'm coming home now!
back:
Kya bakwaas ho rahi hai? Main abhi ghar aa raha hoon!

Kyā bakvās ho rahī hai? Maiṁ abhī ghar ā rahā hūṁ!

Kyā (What) | bakvās (nonsense/rubbish) | ho rahī hai (is happening) | Maiṁ (I) | abhī (now/right now) | ghar (home) | ā rahā hūṁ (am coming - male)

ghar kī keys (house keys) | bhūl gayā (forgot - past) | bhūl rahā hūṁ (am forgetting - present) | bhūl jāūṅgā (will forget - future)

ek delicious cocktail | banāyā (made - past) | banā rahā hūṁ (am making - present) | banāūṅgā (will make - future)

front: The princess said that she wanted Arjun to make her painting.
back:

Princess ne batāyā ki vo palace kī life se tired thī aur freedom chāhtī thī

Princess ne (subject marker) | batāyā (told/shared) | ki (that) | vo (she) | palace kī life se (from palace life) | tired thī (was tired) | aur (and) | freedom (freedom) | chāhtī thī (wanted)

front: There is no gravity in space, so everything and every person floats.
back:
Space me gravity nahi hoti (hai), isliye har cheez aur har insaan float karta hai

Space meṁ gravity nahīṁ hotī (hai), isliye har chīz aur har insān float kartā hai

Space meṁ (in space) | gravity (gravity) | nahīṁ hotī (does not exist/happen) | isliye (that's why/so) | har chīz (everything) | aur (and) | har insān (every person) | float kartā hai (floats)

front: On the space station, there is a strict schedule every day.
back:
Space station par har din ek strict schedule hota hai

Space station par har din ek strict schedule hotā hai

Space station par (on space station) | har din (every day) | ek (a) | strict schedule (strict schedule) | hotā hai (exists/happens)

front: To prevent body muscle loss, they have to exercise for at least two hours daily.
back:
Body muscle loss ko prevent karne (rokne) ke liye unhe daily kam se kam do ghante exercise karna padta hai

Body muscle loss ko prevent karne (rokne) ke liye unheṁ daily kam se kam do ghaṇṭe exercise karnā paṛtā hai

Body muscle loss ko (body muscle loss) | rokne ke liye (to prevent) | unheṁ (they/them) | daily (daily) | kam se kam (at least) | do ghaṇṭe (two hours) | exercise karnā paṛtā hai (have to exercise)

front: To sleep at night, astronauts use sleeping bags that are tied to walls.
back:
Raat ko sone ke liye, astronauts sleeping bags use karte hain jo walls se tied hote hain

Rāt ko sone ke liye, astronauts sleeping bags use karte haiṁ jo walls se tied hote haiṁ

Rāt ko (at night) | sone ke liye (to sleep) | astronauts (astronauts) | sleeping bags (sleeping bags) | use karte haiṁ (use) | jo (which) | walls se (to walls) | tied hote haiṁ (are tied)

front: I have a banana. You have an apple. We have a bomb.
back:
Mere paas ek kela hai. Tumhare paas ek seb hai. Humare paas ek bomb hai.

Mere pās ek kelā hai. Tumhāre pās ek seb hai. Hamāre pās ek bomb hai.

Mere pās (To me/With me) | ek (one) | kelā (banana) | hai (is). Tumhāre pās (To you/With you) | ek (one) | seb (apple) | hai (is). Hamāre pās (To us/With us) | ek (one) | bomb (bomb) | hai (is).

Note: "Tumhāre" is oblique form due to "pās", so it can't become "tumhārī" for instance.

front: My brother is here, my sister is there, and these are my books.
back:
Mera bhai yahaan hai, meri behen wahaan hai, aur ye mere books hain.

Merā bhāī yahāṁ hai, merī bahan vahāṁ hai, aur ye mere books haiṁ.

Merā (My - masc. sing.) | bhāī (brother) | yahāṁ (here) | hai (is), merī (my - fem. sing.) | bahan (sister) | vahāṁ (there) | hai (is), aur (and) | ye (these) | mere (my - masc. plur.) | books | haiṁ (are).

back:
Kya aaj tumhare paas beer ke liye time hai?

Kyā āj tumhāre pās beer ke liye time hai?

Kyā (Question marker) | āj (today) | tumhāre pās (with you / to you) | beer | ke liye (for) | time | hai (is)?

front: She is sitting on the chair.
back:
Vo chair par baithi hai.

Vo chair par baiṭhī hai.

Vo (She) | chair par (on the chair) | baiṭhī hai (is sitting - feminine)

front: I am coming from home.
back:
Main ghar se aa raha hoon.

Maiṁ ghar se ā rahā hūṁ.

Maiṁ (I) | ghar (home) | se (from) | ā rahā hūṁ (am coming - masculine)

front: I read (past tense) a lot, that's why I passed.
back:
Main bahut padha, isliye pass ho gaya.

Maiṁ bahut paṛhā, isliye pass ho gayā.

Maiṁ (I) | bahut (a lot) | paṛhā (read/studied - past) | isliye (that's why / so) | pass ho gayā (passed / got passed)

Note: "Maiṁ" not "maine" because there's no direct object for "paṛhā"

front: I want to play guitar, but I don't have time.
back:
Main guitar bajaana chahta hoon, lekin mere paas time nahi hai.

Maiṁ guitar bajānā chāhtā hūṁ, lekin mere pās time nahīṁ hai.

Maiṁ (I) | guitar (guitar) | bajānā (to play - instrument) | chāhtā hūṁ (want - male speaker) | lekin (but) | mere pās (with me / I have) | time (time) | nahīṁ hai (don't have)

Maiṁ (I) | kūd saktā hūṁ (can jump) | maiṁ (I) | kūd saktā thā (could jump) | maiṁ (I) | kūd sakūṅgā (will be able to jump)

Mujhe thoṛā time chāhiye thā.

Mujhe (To me) | thoṛā (a little) | time (time) | chāhiye thā (was needed)

front: You needed my help. (informal)
back:

Mujhe vo song pasand thā/āyā.

Mujhe (To me) | vo (that) | song (song - masc) | pasand thā/āyā (was liked / appealed)

front: I think I will like Norwich.

Mujhe lagta hai mujhe Norwich pasand aayega.

Mujhe lagtā hai mujhe Norwich pasand āegā.

Mujhe (To me) | lagtā hai (it feels/I think) | mujhe (to me) | Norwich (Norwich) | pasand āegā (will come to be liked)

back:
Mujhe pata hai ki tum aaj busy ho.

Mujhe patā hai ki tum āj busy ho.

Mujhe (to me) | patā hai (known is) | ki (that) | tum (you) | āj (today) | busy (busy) | ho (are)

front: This is Shivani's guitar now, therefore I don't have a guitar anymore.
back:
Ab ye Shivani ki guitar hai, isliye mere paas ab guitar nahi hai.

Ab ye Shivani kī guitar hai, isliye mere pās ab guitar nahīṁ hai.

Ab (now) | ye (this) | Shivani (Shivani) | kī ('s / of [feminine agreement]) | guitar (guitar) | hai (is) | isliye (therefore) | mere pās (with me / I have) | ab (now) | guitar (guitar) | nahīṁ hai (not is)

Ho sakta hai ki vo busy ho.

Ho saktā hai ki vo busy ho.

Agar tum is weekend free hote, toh Norwich me milna accha hota.

Agar tum is weekend free hote, toh Norwich meṁ milnā acchā hotā.

12 baje tak apnā homework khatam karo, varnā maiṁ tumheṁ 1 baje ek thappaṛ mārūṅgā!

2. Use (to her) | patā hai (is known) | ki (that) | maiṁ (I) | jhūṭhā hūṁ (am a liar)

back:
Mujhe coffee me zyaada cheeni pasand nahi hai.

Mujhe coffee meṁ zyādā chīnī pasand nahīṁ hai.

Mujhe (to me) | coffee meṁ (in coffee) | zyādā chīnī (too much sugar) | pasand nahīṁ hai (is not liked / don't like)

Tum door band karo.

back:

  • His/Hers (near): Ye billi iski hai.
  • His/Hers (far): Ye billi uski hai.
  • Ours: Ye billi hamaari hai.
  • Theirs: Ye billi unki hai.

front: I take a little rest after lunch.

Main lunch ke baad thoda rest karta hoon.

Maiṁ lunch ke bād thoṛā rest kartā hūṁ.
